justification: Round-2 re-check only, per the gauntlet's narrow scope: round 1 already scored 9.3 with a full verify-page pass (Lighthouse 100/100/100/100, zero console errors, zero broken links across 34 internal / 6 external), and the round-2 writer pass touched exactly two things, both technical-only: (1) the 'Building a heap from n elements is O(n), not O(n log n)' section's prose (around the constructor-cost paragraph and the Sedgewick/Wayne + CLRS citation paragraph) was revised, and (2) a 2-line guard clause was added to IndexedMinHeap.DecreaseKey plus matching prose in the trailing exercise-solution paragraph. `node tools/run-code.mjs` on the article confirms PASS (blocks=23 executed=10), so nothing broke compilation or expected output. On design specifically: the prose edits are ordinary paragraph text with only short inline code spans (`SiftDown`, `h / 2^(h+1)`, `BUILD-MAX-HEAP`, `SiftUp`, all well under the 25-character inline-code-wrap threshold), and prose reflows at any viewport width, so there is no mobile clipping risk there. The new guard clause sits inside the exercise's `csharp run id=indexed-heap` code block (itself inside a collapsed `:::solution`, so it isn't shown by default): `if (_comparer.Compare(newPriority, _priorities[i]) >= 0)` (64 chars) shows its operative comparison — 'newPriority' being compared — within the ~40 visible characters before the phone fade; the `throw new ArgumentException(...)` line (119 chars) fades out well before its message string, but per WRITER_GUIDE.md's rule ('longer lines are fine when the tail is boilerplate; not fine when the tail is the point'), the message text is boilerplate — the guard's actual meaning ('reject any newPriority that isn't strictly smaller than what's already stored') is stated in the very next sentence of the solution's explanatory prose, which a phone reader reaches immediately after the code block. Neither new line causes page-level horizontal overflow (code blocks scroll sideways inside their own box by design, per WRITER_GUIDE section 7). No figure, table, or callout was touched by this pass. Score is unchanged from round 1: nothing regressed and nothing new was introduced that would move the score.
